title: SOC2 prep: personal scratchpad and control-question backlog
content:
Quick personal scratchpad for SOC2 prep — dump of open questions, mapping ideas, and evidence notes. Not for sharing yet; will sanitize before handing to auditor or C-Suite.

Top-level objectives (handy reminder):
- baseline current control coverage across Hosted / Dedicated / Private deployments
- short-list gaps that require engineering work vs. policy evidence only
- assemble an evidence collection plan with owners and deadlines (aim: internal readiness review 2026-03-15)

Open questions / uncertainties:
- Encryption key lifecycle: where do we have automated rotation vs. manual? Private deployments: customers manage KMS, but we must show separation of duties for control A.3. Need a short note of exceptions.
- Logical access reviews cadence: quarterly? Who signs off currently for infra accounts (SRE lead or infra manager)? Ticketing trail is scattered — need to centralize in Confluence page.
- Change management for runtime kernels: do our rollout docs + canary policy (Console) satisfy CC change control requirements or do we need a separate changelog artifact for auditors?

Control mapping draft (very rough):
- CC: Access Controls --> evidence: IAM reports, quarterly access review notes, SSO audit logs (ok for hosted API)
- CC: System Configuration --> evidence: infra-as-code PR history, release tags, config drift scans (scripts in infra repo)
- CC: Logical & Physical Separation (Dedicated/Private) --> evidence: network diagrams, VPC boundary docs, customer contract language for on-prem option
- CC: Backup & Recovery --> evidence: backup schedules, restore test runbook (need last restore test date)

Immediate action items (priority order):
1) Ask SRE for exported IAM CSV and last 2 quarterly review minutes (owner: Ethan) — target 2026-02-24
2) Locate the last restore test artifact (where is the runbook?) — owner: Jordan — target 2026-02-20
3) Draft short explainer of canary/fallback policy for auditors (2 pages) — owner: Asha — target 2026-03-01
4) Compile list of all KMS integrations and note whether rotation is customer-managed or Redwood-managed — owner: Jordan/Asha — target 2026-02-28

Evidence formatting notes (auditor-friendly):
- Prefer time-stamped exports (CSV/JSON) with short README describing filters used.
- When pulling screenshots, include UTC timestamp and path to source.
- Annotate PR excerpts that show approvals/CI green statuses; auditors like a single-page index that points to raw artifacts.

Risks I keep circling back to:
- Patch windows: we do rolling upgrades but don't have a standardized list of systems we patch vs. vendor-managed. Might surface as a gap under change control.
- Dev creds in long-lived scripts: need a harvest of repos that contain service-account keys; spike to find worst offenders.
- Third-party subprocessing: some monitoring logs are forwarded to a hosted provider — confirm any overlap with SOC2 data categories.

Notes-to-self / next thoughts:
- Make a short template: control -> evidence types -> owner -> single artifact link -> note (why sufficient). Use this to build the control matrix.
- Consider a 30-min sync with product security to validate the "model serving" control descriptions (auditors will ask: how do you protect model input/output?).
- Add a line-item for Dedicated SLAs: ensure contractual evidence exists for uptime targets claimed in sales decks.

Random scratch ideas:
- Could we export a 90-day summary snapshot of cost/latency dashboards as a proxy for availability SLOs? Might help for operational effectiveness evidence.
- For Private deployments, collect a sanitized sample of deployment manifests to show that customers run non-privileged containers (if applicable).

End of scratchpad (for now). Will prune and copy into shared control matrix once I confirm owners and gather raw artifacts.

Last quick log: 2026-02-18 08:30 — dropped a note to Ethan in Slack (SRE) about IAM export. Waiting on reply.
